reports.summary: I handled every (e) and (f) item and re-checked the earlier (a)–(d) fixes on the current tree; they still hold. Live finding: when ← was pressed repeatedly, the OSD text was wrong and the seek bar was right. The bridge worked out the OSD time itself, from vlc_player_GetTime(), which ignores a seek that has not landed yet; an arrow's jump also runs later on the input thread. So the second press printed the old time minus one jump ('00:48' while the bar showed 00:38). The fix: the OSD now shows the exact target the core seeks to, which a seek-only player timer (on_seek) reports, in the order the hotkeys were pressed. I added a native regression test to bridge-smoke (fixture suite). Against the old bridge it fails ('00:01 / 00:02' instead of '00:02 / 00:02'); with the fix it passes. The play control after the end of the media is right: STOPPED with the media kept draws the orange Play tile, and pressing it starts the item again. A new test checks both what is drawn and the command sent. S34.Player/music: the waveform is opt-in under D028. Evidence: the video's Playback tab at 09m17.5 shows the toggle OFF, and the transcript at 12:00 says 'the waveform seekbar if you want'. So the screen entry keeps the solid default and records a D028 deviation. A new entry, S34.Player/music-waveform, renders the opt-in, and its waveform matches Figma apart from the D048 head. What still FAILs in both entries is window and bar backgrounds off by 2/255, which are not in my files. D028 now cites this evidence, and VIDEO_BREAKDOWN line 138 no longer lists bar-icon hover as OPEN. Re-checks on the current tree: C.SeekBar/default, S01.ControlBar/default, C.PlayButton play/pause, C.CurrentTime and C.Duration default/remaining all PASS. S34.ControlBar/music, S21.Timeline/default, C.SeekPreview and C.VolumeTooltip are REVIEW. The OSD render is still correct (outline, sits left of the queue panel). Tests: ControlBarParityTests (10, one new), FigmaDeviationTests, PlayerInteractionTests (the earlier Customize-row failure is now fixed by its owner), OSDLayout, OSDTypography, SeekProgressRedraw, PlayerProgressRegression, MiniPlayerSeekBinding, ConeScrollIsolation, PauseButtonContrast, Scrubbing and the GalleryRenderTests catalog checks all pass. swift build is clean.
fixed: (f) Live: OSD '00:48' while the bar read 00:38 during repeated ← seeks. The OSD was wrong. MXRHotkeyFeedback.inc predicted the target from vlc_player_GetTime (seeking=false), which misses a seek still in flight, and an arrow's jump runs later on the input thread. Jump and arrow actions now wait for MXRFeedbackAwaitSeek. MXRServicesBridge registers a seek-only player timer (on_seek gives the core's exact target, as vlc_player_input_SeekByTime prints it) and posts '<target> / <length>' for each pending jump hotkey, in order, within 1 s. Seeks from the seek bar produce no OSD. Regression test in module/tests/bridge-smoke.m: two synchronous jump+extrashort (1 s) presses while paused. New test ControlBarParityTests.testPlayControlAfterTheEndShowsPlayAndRestarts checks the drawn tile colour before and after, and the command. It is a guard test: there was no bug to fix in my files. D-menus' SpaceAfterEndTests covers Space.

Builds and tests:

- The targeted suites all pass: ControlBarParity, FigmaDeviation, PlayerInteraction, OSDLayout, OSDTypography, SeekProgressRedraw, PlayerProgressRegression, MiniPlayerSeekBinding, ConeScrollIsolation, PauseButtonContrast, Scrubbing and the GalleryRender catalog checks. - I ran the native fixture suite on the real tree, under the lock, and released the lock. It passes, including bridge-smoke with the new jump OSD test. This means the compile problem the fixer reported for MXRAudioPreferenceServices.m is gone at HEAD. Log: native-fixture.log in the same folder.
- I did not reproduce the "fails without the fix" step myself. The fixer's before log (../build/evidence/final4/B-controls/native-fixture-before.log) shows the exact new failure message, "00:02 / 00:02, not 00:01 / 00:02".

The OSD fix (live finding '00:48' while the bar read 00:38) has the right root cause:
- In src/player/input.c, vlc_player_input_SeekByTime adds the jump to vlc_player_input_GetTime(seeking=true) and calls vlc_player_UpdateTimerSeekState. That sends the target to on_seek through timer.c.
- The old code predicted the target from vlc_player_GetTime, which does not see a seek still in flight.
- The bridge now waits for on_seek. The callback ignores the NULL value sent when a seek ends. Commands are asserted to run on main, so the pending counter is updated before the queued seek reports arrive. The timer is added and removed in init and shutdown, and dealloc asserts it is gone.

issues.description: The jump OSD matches on_seek reports to hotkey presses only by count and a 1 s deadline. Within that second, a different seek can take a pending slot: a seek-bar seek, a chapter or title seek (player.c UpdateChapterSeekState also calls UpdateTimerSeekState), or the next seek after a jump whose input_ControlPush failed. An arrow press followed at once by a chapter key could then show the chapter's time, and the arrow's target would be dropped. This is an edge case and does not affect the live finding. A fix would tag the expected target or clear the pending count on non-jump actions.

The disabled-control dimming uses a literal opacity of 0.4 instead of a token. It predates this wave (commit 3d1fbcbfd3). Theme.Popup.disabledOpacity, or a player token, should be used to meet the tokens-only rule.

Both entries still FAIL on flat colours 2/255 off: the window backdrop is #1B1B1B vs #1D1D1D (D053 explains this as the cover-art glow) and the bar is bgA4 #191919 vs Figma's homeCard #171717 in Player - Music. These are outside B-controls' files. The bar-colour difference is not covered by a decision; it belongs to the bar's owner.
